title: Constraint systems require going outside the system to find their patterns

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Constraint systems require going outside the system to find their patterns

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Unlike rule-based systems, which can be run directly, systems defined by constraints offer no direct procedure for finding the patterns they allow; one must search from outside the system, which can take enormous computational effort.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But in a system that is based on constraints, there is no such direct procedure, and instead one must in effect always go outside of the system to work out what patterns can occur.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Systems Based on Constraints” (from p. 210), p. 217. Scope: systems defined by constraints versus explicit evolution rules

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Restricted families permit precise algorithmic comparisons, but the universal procedural contrast is not itself well-defined. Public algorithms and theory resolve examples rather than the broad statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define directness by a fixed algorithmic model and compare the time needed to generate trajectories under evolution rules with the time needed to find satisfying configurations for matched constraint families. Complexity lower bounds or efficient constructive algorithms would test restricted formal versions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Constraint satisfaction ranges from trivial to undecidable.

“Going outside the system” is metaphorical.

No single complexity statement covers all constraint systems.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The text says there is no direct procedure because the system is given by constraints, which is the definition of that setup rather than a further fact. Nearby theorems about tiling being undecidable are stronger than anything this paragraph states, and the same section says that with tricks the examples at hand are feasible. No measurement distinguishes the sentence from the definition it restates.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A constraint system is defined by allowed local templates rather than by an update rule, so the absence of a built-in evolution step restates that definition. Enormous effort has no cutoff that would separate this contrast from ordinary search.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Enormous computational effort names no complexity bound and no class of instances.

The sentence contrasts a constraint with an explicit update rule, which is how the two setups are defined.
